result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, and the new tests pass.

**Change** — `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`: I replaced the two mock rules (`.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*`) with one rule, `.*/(__)?mock[^/]*/.*`. The `[^/]*` lets the folder name carry any characters, including punctuation, non-ASCII, or nothing after `mock`. The slash on each side keeps the match inside one folder, so `remock/` and `demo/` don't match and `mock.java` (a file, not a folder) doesn't either. Backslash paths work because `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already tries slash-normalized variants of the path.

**Test** — new `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`: checks the new folder names (`mock`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟`, `__mock`, backslash paths) and the old ones (`mocks`, `__mocks__`, `mock-data`, `mock_data`, `mock data`, `mockStore`), plus the non-matches (`remock`, `demo`, `src/main/java`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`).

**Verification:** `mvn -q -o -pl codeanalyzer test -Dtest=ScopingConventionsTest,SourceFileFilterTest` passes (2 + 6 tests). I did not run the full module test suite.

Nothing is committed.
